head: 0355023c3170c87a84cd9e5688ae6b4f3e4df3ae
summary: Four threads traced at the exact head with one build-level lab. Ranked: (1) CONCRETE BUILD FINDING: -PdisableJsClient=true does not remove the Scalar npm dependency; the WAR graph still runs node/npm and embeds the 3.5 MB bundle (dry-run verified), unlike the generated JS client, which the flag does remove. (2) CONCRETE BEHAVIOR DIVERGENCE: on an expired or revoked credential the explorer replays the dead Authorization header indefinitely if its own request hits the 401 first; unlike the Admin UI interceptor, nothing clears the header or routes to login inside the explorer. Recovery is via re-login in the Admin UI, after which the explorer recovers without a reload. JWT rides the same storage key and behaves identically (source-traced; no JWT lab). (3) METADATA: the shared OpenAPI spec declares a single relative server URL '/api' with no variables; the generated Java, JavaScript, and Python clients consume it with generator defaults, so the webapp context path and any proxy prefix live entirely outside the spec. (4) FRAMING: the strict headers sit only on /index.html; the Scalar page is served without them by design of the embed, and sessionStorage's origin scoping is what protects the credential. No vulnerability is claimed anywhere in this report.
findings: THREAD 4/finding 1 (build, dry-run verified): settings.gradle:70 computes withJsClient from -PdisableJsClient; solr/webapp/build.gradle line 54 wires the generated JS client bundle only under that flag, but line 61 wires scalarBundle (project :solr:webapp:scalar) unconditionally, and the war block (lines 150-154) always copies it into libs/scalar. The scalar project's build.gradle.kts has exactly one content task chain: an NpmTask 'npm install @scalar/api-reference@<pinned>' plus a Sync of dist/browser/standalone.js (3.5 MB). Dry runs of :solr:webapp:war at this head (evidence tarball): with -PdisableJsClient=true every js-client task disappears while :solr:webapp:scalar:nodeSetup, npmSetup, downloadScalarApiReference, and copyScalarBundle all remain. So a node-less or offline build still fails on this module, and the flag's promise (no JS client toolchain) holds only for the generated client. Smallest change: apply the same withJsClient condition to the scalarBundle wiring and the war copy, or document the exception in the flag's help text; if the bundle is omitted, the API Explorer entry should degrade cleanly (its iframe target would 404). Provenance: the bundle is a prebuilt third-party artifact fetched from the npm registry at build time (comment in build.gradle.kts: 'Keeps the large generated bundle out of source control'), pinned at 1.46.4 in gradle/libs.versions.toml; there is no solr/licenses entry for it, unlike the Java dependencies. Runtime network behavior is closed off by configuration in scalar-init.js: telemetry false, withDefaultFonts false, agent disabled, proxyUrl empty.

THREAD 1/finding 2 (credentials, source-traced against services.js/app.js/login.js and the branch's scalar-init.js): the fix's onBeforeRequest reads sessionStorage 'auth.header' fresh on every same-origin request, so the explorer always presents the UI's CURRENT credential and never caches one of its own. The Admin UI interceptor (app.js responseError ~line 446; services.js ~line 58) treats a 401 as session death: it sets http401, DELETES auth.header, and the app routes to the login screen. The explorer has no equivalent: if an explorer request is the first to meet a 401 (expired password, revoked user, rotated credential), Scalar simply renders the 401 response in its pane and keeps replaying the same dead header on subsequent requests, with no redirect and no clearing. If instead any Admin UI request meets the 401 first, auth.header is deleted and the explorer then sends NO Authorization header (still with X-Requested-With, so no browser Basic popup) and shows 401s until re-login. Either way recovery is: log in again in the Admin UI (login.js rewrites auth.header), and the explorer then works on its next request without being reloaded. 403 (authenticated, not authorized) is special-cased by neither side; Scalar renders the 403 body. This is a consistency/UX divergence, not a credential leak: the header lives in the user's own origin-scoped sessionStorage in both designs.

THREAD 1 (JWT): login.js line ~153 stores 'Bearer <accessToken>' into the SAME auth.header key for the JWT/OAuth flow, and the explorer's hook is scheme-blind, so JWT presentation and expiry behavior are identical to Basic by construction. No JWT lab was run: the webapp Selenium harness configures BasicAuthPlugin only, and no claim beyond the shared code path is made.

THREAD 2/finding 3 (OpenAPI metadata, traced plus built artifact read): solr/api's ApiMetadata.java line 34 declares servers = @Server(url = '/api'). The generated spec built at this head (solr/api/build/generated/openapi/solr-openapi-11.0.0-SNAPSHOT.json) carries exactly "servers": [{"url": "/api", "description": "This Solr node"}], OpenAPI 3.0.1. solr/api/build.gradle generates the Java client (consumed by SolrJ via the openapiSpec artifact), a JavaScript client (openapi-generator 'javascript', package 'solr'), and a Python client ('python', package 'solr'), all with generator defaults and no server/basePath overrides; the webapp war also renames this spec to libs/scalar/spec.json for the explorer. Concrete effects: the '/api' suffix is baked into every client's base path while the deployment prefix (the '/solr' context path, or any proxy mount) appears nowhere in the metadata and has no template variable, so client users and proxy deployers must compose the full base themselves; the explorer sidesteps this because Scalar resolves the relative URL against the serving origin. Proxy path-prefix assumption, stated as a source-grounded consequence rather than a lab result: the branch's onBeforeRequest attaches credentials only when the request URL's origin equals the page origin; a proxy that serves the UI and the API under DIFFERENT origins therefore silently strips the Authorization header and every explorer request fails 401, while a same-origin path-prefix proxy preserves the behavior (subject to composing the '/api' base correctly). The split-origin case was not lab-run.

THREAD 3/finding 4 (framing and proxy variants, source-traced; default packaged behavior already evidenced in the r2 gate receipts): LoadAdminUiServlet sets X-Frame-Options: DENY and a CSP with frame-ancestors 'none' and frame-src 'self', and web.xml maps that servlet ONLY to /index.html. The Scalar page (libs/scalar/index.html, framed by partials/api-explorer.html) is served as a static resource WITHOUT those headers, which is precisely what makes the same-origin embed work while the UI page itself stays unframable (SOLR-7966). Variants: a path-prefix same-origin proxy preserves the whole policy; a proxy that strips or rewrites response CSP removes the frame-ancestors protection on the UI page (a deployment-side weakening, not a defect in this branch); a split-origin deployment breaks the embed itself because frame-src 'self' no longer covers the Scalar origin. No vulnerability is claimed for the un-headered Scalar page: sessionStorage is origin-scoped, so a foreign page framing it cannot read the user's stored header, and the framed explorer would send only that foreign origin's (empty) storage. Any security concern here belongs to the SECURITY.md process with a reachability proof this investigation did not find.

COORDINATION: this investigation ran in its own clone (solr-clones/5201-inv and a disposable parent clone) and did not modify the selector investigation's checkout, selectors, or evidence; its runs used the same shared Gradle lock sequentially. The selector investigation's result report is filed separately and its conclusions are not duplicated here.
limitations: JWT behavior is source-traced only (harness is Basic-only). Split-origin and header-stripping proxy variants are analyzed from source, not lab-run; the default packaged framing behavior rests on the prior r2 receipts plus the passing harness runs in the sibling investigation. The generated clients were inspected via their build configuration and the built spec, not executed.
evidence: records/evidence/pr-5201-adjacent-investigation-20261111-evidence.tar.gz (SHA-256 9e48fc3f196b4d8d564440da3f23abd04140869b534a071a371f10761db2b9fe): the disableJsClient vs default war dry-run logs. All other citations are file and line references at the head named above.
